name: Maintenance page
summary: A planned-downtime page that says what is paused, that nothing is lost, and when it will be back, in the person's time zone.
use: during planned maintenance, when part or all of the product is paused
a11y: The return time is a time element with a machine-readable datetime; the status link and email option are real links and buttons.
notes: Show the return time in the person's own time zone and keep the minutes left current; Email me when it's back is an action for your app to wire.

use_when: planned work pauses the product or one area of it
a deploy needs the app read-only for a known time
avoid_when: an unplanned outage with no known end: use page-error with a status link
only a small feature is paused: use a warning banner (page-banners)

parts.name: title
parts.what: the heading: what happened, in plain words, as in “Invoices are paused for an upgrade”

parts.name: message
parts.what: one or two sentences: what it means and what to do next, as in “We're upgrading the payments database. Everythin”

parts.name: until
parts.what: when it will be back, as a time element, as in “3:00 PM UTC”

parts.name: detail
parts.what: a short line of detail under the title, as in “Saturday, Nov 14 · about 40 minutes from now”

parts.name: notify
parts.what: the Email me when it's back action

empty.how: Not applicable: this state screen shows no list of records.

loading.how: Not applicable: this page stands in for content; it isn't loaded data itself.

error.how: The part is itself an error or system state, written in plain words with a next step.

disabled.how: No control here is ever disabled; each one always does something.

overflow.how: Actions stack full width under 30rem; the panel caps its width.

long_text.how: Titles balance and body text wraps at word boundaries inside a capped measure.

keyboard: Tab moves through the links and buttons in reading order
Enter follows a link; Enter or Space presses a button
